b.like: like the p in “spin” (no puff of air)
b.tip: Not a puffed p: say “spin”, then drop the s.

p.like: like the p in “pin”, with a big puff
p.tip: A tissue held at your lips should flick.

t.like: like the t in “top”, with a big puff

k.like: like the k in “kite”, with a big puff

h.like: like the h in “hat”, but raspier
h.tip: Raise the back of your tongue, a little like the ch in Scottish “loch”.

j.tip: Tongue tip down behind your bottom teeth, lips spread. Not curled (that's zh).

q.like: like the ch in “cheese”, smiling, with a puff
q.tip: Never “kw” as in “queen”. Tongue tip down behind your bottom teeth.

x.like: like the sh in “sheet”, said with a smile
x.tip: Between s and sh, tongue tip behind your bottom teeth. Never “ks” or “z”.

zh.like: like the j in “judge”, tongue pulled back
zh.tip: No puff. Tongue a little further back than English j; tip up.

ch.like: like the ch in “church”, tongue pulled back, with a puff
ch.tip: Tip up and back (q is tip down and smiling).

sh.like: like the sh in “shop”, tongue pulled back
sh.tip: Don't round your lips; tongue further back than English sh.

r.like: like the s in “measure”, tongue tip curled back
r.tip: Somewhere between English r and the s in “pleasure”. Lips flat, a light buzz; don't roll it.

z.tip: Not the z of “zoo”: start from “ds”.

c.like: like the ts in “cats”, with a puff
c.tip: Never k or s: think “it's hot”.

a.like: “ah”, like an Aussie “car” without the r
a.tip: Drop your jaw; not the a in “cat”.

o.like: a tiny w, then “or” as in “wore”: bo ≈ “bwor”
o.tip: Round your lips; not the “oh” of “boat”.

e.like: “uh”, like “her” without the r, from the back of the throat
e.tip: Relaxed lips. Never the e in “bed”.

u.like: like the oo in “shoot”, lips pushed well forward
u.tip: An Aussie “oo” sits too far forward and drifts towards ü: pull your tongue back and pout hard.

ü.like: say “ee”, then round your lips without moving your tongue
ü.tip: An Aussie “ew” is a fair start. Not “oo”, not “you”.

ei.like: like the “ay” in “eight”, starting from the e in “bed”
ei.tip: An Aussie “ay” starts too open and sounds like ai.

ou.like: like “oh”, with rounded lips: “or” sliding to “oo”
ou.tip: An Aussie “oh” starts with flat lips: round them from the start.

en.tip: A lazy “uhn”, not the en in “Ben”.

eng.tip: Keep a lazy “uh”; don't let it become ang.

ong.tip: Not the “ong” of “song”: round your lips to “oo”.

er.like: say “uh” and curl your tongue tip back as you say it
er.tip: Like an American “are”. Your Aussie “ah” needs the curl.

ie.tip: One quick glide, not “ee-eh” in two beats.

iou.tip: iu is short for iou: there's a little o in it.

ian.tip: Not “yan”: the a here sounds like e.

uei.tip: ui is short for uei: there's a little e in it. Not “gwee”.

uen.tip: un is short for uen. Not “doon”.

üe.like: ü then “eh”: xué ≈ “shweh” with your lips pouted

üan.tip: It's ü, and the a sounds like e. Not “wahn”.

ün.tip: Tongue as for “ee”, lips as for “oo”. Not “yoon”.

i-z.like: no “ee”: just hold the buzz of the sound before it (zì ≈ “dzz”, sì ≈ “sss”)
i-z.tip: Don't move your tongue after the z, c or s.

i-zh.like: hold the curled sound and hum through it (shì ≈ “shrr”)
i-zh.tip: Not “she”: your tongue stays curled back.

r.like: curl your tongue tip back at the end

tones.0: light and short, no tone of its own
tones.1: high and level, like holding a note
tones.3: low; on its own it dips and comes back up a little, in a sentence it just stays low

traps.say: uen (dùn ≈ “dwun”), but ün after j, q, x and y (jūn, yún)

traps.spelling: u after j, q, x, y
traps.say: ü: jù, qù, xué, yuǎn. The dots stay only after n and l (nǚ, lǜ).
only spelling: yī = i, wǔ = u, yú = ü, yǒu = iou, wèi = uei
“uh” on its own (hē); “ay” in ei; “eh” in ie and üe; a lazy “uh” in en and eng. Never the e in “bed”.
the a sounds like e: “yen”, “ywen”. So ian isn't iang.
“ee” (nǐ); just a buzz after z, c, s (sì); a curled hum after zh, ch, sh, r (shì isn't “she”)

traps.spelling: o after b, p, m, f
b d g j zh z / p t k q ch c
traps.say: the difference is the puff of air, not the buzz
-n ends with the tongue tip behind the top teeth; -ng with the back of the tongue up

traps.spelling: j q x / zh ch sh
traps.say: tongue tip down and smiling, or tongue pulled back (xiè vs shéi)
